summary: Chebucto Head Light, on the southwest side of the entrance to Halifax Harbour, was first shown in 1872; the present concrete octagonal tower dates from 1967.

structures.note: Square wooden tower of about 22 ft 6 in (LF quoting the 1872 report), painted white, with the keeper's dwelling attached.
LF: built 1930 for $16,900 by A.S. MacMillan of Halifax. NSLPS: a concrete tower with a red lantern built about 1928. Both: destroyed about 1940 for a gun battery.
Square white two-storey dwelling with a red lantern room (LF); NSLPS calls it the third lighthouse, a cupola lighthouse. Burned in May 2004.
White octagonal concrete tower with a red top (CCG); red aluminium lantern (NSLPS).

access.note: Grounds open; tower closed. Road gated because of vandalism; visitors park at the gate and walk in (NSLPS; LF).

events.note: First shown 21 August 1872 (LF, quoting the Department's report for 1872).
Square wooden tower with dwelling attached; contract to Jacob Bowser for $2,375.
Steam whistle in a red-brick fog-alarm building, first run 1 June 1892 (LF).
Submarine bell, cables to two tripods off the headland; in operation by the year to June 1906 (LF; Department report).
Four flashes in 30 seconds changed to four flashes in 20 seconds (report for the year to June 1922). The CCG list now gives Fl W 20s; the sources do not explain the difference.
Concrete octagonal tower and two dwellings, contract $16,900 (LF). NSLPS dates the second concrete tower to about 1928.
Concrete tower destroyed at the onset of the Second World War, site needed for a gun battery (LF; NSLPS: about 1940).
Site taken for a gun battery; the wartime dwelling-lighthouse was built in its place (LF; NSLPS).
Square white two-storey dwelling with red lantern room, cost $16,940 (LF).
One-and-a-half-storey dwelling for an assistant keeper (LF).
New fog-alarm building erected; the old red-brick building went to the military at Fort Chebucto for a demolition exercise (LF).
Current concrete octagonal tower completed (LF; NSLPS; CCG).
Automated by the time Stanley Flemming retired in 1980 (LF: 'it wasn't long before the station was automated'). NSLPS: keepers of the 1940 dwelling took part in 1970s automation programmes.
A dwelling removed from the station (LF).
Chebucto Head Lighthouse Society formed by local people to preserve the buildings (LF).
The 1940 keeper's dwelling burned in May 2004 (24/25 May per NSLPS); judged suspicious (LF; NSLPS).

wrecks.outcome: Stranded at Chebucto Head. Department's buoy steamer Lady Laurier took 600 passengers from the steamer to Halifax; the wreck list records the master as found negligent and suspended for three months. Duncan's Cove's report gives its own call-out as 17 January.
Ashore at Chebucto Head in thick fog and heavy sea. Duncan's Cove lifeboat stood by until the crew landed in their own boat; the Herring Cove boat was forced to return after hours pulling.
Herring Cove boat called out to the wreck at Chebucto Head in a stiff gale; forced to return after pulling for some hours. Whether this is the same vessel as the 1912 schooner is not stated.
Stranded and lost on Chebucto Head, Halifax harbour; registered at Halifax, official no. 106075. Formal investigation at Halifax on 17 June 1916.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LF says the 1940 two-storey dwelling had served as the lighthouse for many years and that the current concrete tower was completed in 1967, so the 1967 deactivation in the record fits the switch to the new tower. No source gives a separate deactivation date.

The record lists 1872 (first light, Rowlett) and 1940 and 1967 (later towers). The sources agree on 1872 for the first light and on the 1967 tower; the 1940 and 1930 towers are separate structures in the sequence.
Lighthouse Friends gives Richard Holland to 1929 and Edward Gallagher from 1929. The NSLPS keeper list gives 1928 for both. The story gives the LF dates and says NSLPS dates the change to 1928.

notes_for_editor: Keeper names are spelt as LF gives them: Edward Johnson in the keeper list, Edwin Johnson in LF's quotation of the 1872 report; not resolved. The 1930 concrete tower: LF gives 1930 and a $16,900 contract; NSLPS gives 'about 1928' and says it had a red lantern. The story gives both. The Isleworth: a schooner in the 1912 report, a steamer ('ss.') in the 1913 report, both at Chebucto Head on 13 and 15 March; the sources do not say whether these are one vessel. The Uranium: the Lady Laurier account and the wreck list give 12 January 1913; the Duncan's Cove call-out gives 17 January. The 1922 change: four flashes in 30 s to four flashes in 20 s, but the CCG list now gives a single flash every 20 s (Fl W 20s); the sources do not explain the change. The Duncan's Cove coxswain John Holland (1899-1900 report) is not linked to the lightkeeper Richard Holland. The Department's keepers' table for 1908-09 is OCR-aligned: 'Capt. Richard Holland Oct. 1, 1906' is matched to Chebucto Head by its position in the same row block, which the checker should confirm against the page image. The Nova Scotia Archives caption says 'Mrs. Gallager' without a first name; matching it to Catherine Gallagher is an inference from the place and LF's account. LF dates Creighton's visit to 1943; the photograph is dated about 1949. Private residents (the caretakers named by LF and NSLPS) are not named. Stanley Flemming is named only in his public role as keeper, with dates from LF; personal details from LF and NSLPS are left out. Not run: a Chronicling America search for the 1913 Uranium stranding (one search returned unrelated pages); a US newspaper confirmation would strengthen the wreck entries. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the Chebucto Head row of the 1909 keepers' table (scan 166, printed 159) was checked on the page image and reads Chebucto Head Light and Fog Alarm | Capt. Richard Holland | Oct. 1, 1906 on one line. The 1906-07 list (scan 181, printed 172) also shows Holland, Richard at Chibucto Head Light and Fog Alarm with Oct 1, 1906 on the image. The 1912 Isleworth (lifeboat stood by) and the 1913 Uranium call-out (Duncan's Cove, 17 January) were checked on the scans. The 1872 height is given in metres first with the fraction as LF prints it; the cached copy holds a replacement character where the fraction should be.
